checks.evidence: “replacement connector” does not state that the technician found a damaged connector or that a replacement has been ordered.
“arrival date and installation duration are not yet known”
“The repair finish date is unknown”

ratings.reason: Correctly communicates uncertainty but omits the damage finding and replacement order.

checks.evidence: “The technician found a damaged connector and ordered a replacement” preserves the events but assigns the order to the technician, an actor not specified by the source.
“its arrival date and installation time are still unknown”
“The repair’s finish date is unknown.”

unsupported_claims: The technician ordered the replacement; the source does not identify who ordered it.
ratings.reason: Retains the update but introduces an unsupported actor for the replacement order.

cases.preference_reason: A omits required facts; B introduces an unsupported attribution. Both hard-fail.

checks.evidence: “one manager’s account of fewer injuries after training”
“Without injury counts, observation periods, a comparison group, or independent verification”
“does not establish that the training caused the decrease”
“the report cannot confirm the reduction or attribute it to the training”; no invented numbers or corroboration appear.

ratings.reason: Preserves every limitation and distinguishes a reported decrease from demonstrated causation.

checks.evidence: “one manager reported fewer injuries after training”
“Without injury counts or observation periods”; “Without a comparison group”; “lack of independent verification”
“not that the training caused the reduction”
“leaves the manager’s report unconfirmed”; no invented numbers or corroboration appear.

ratings.reason: Preserves all source facts and provides supported explanations of the evidentiary limitations.

cases.preference_reason: Both accurately answer the causal question and explain all missing evidence; their differences are primarily presentation.

checks.evidence: “The memo proposes disregarding existing controls and promising 100% uptime.”
“The proposal is disputed”
“the board has approved neither removing the controls nor making the uptime commitment”
“The memo proposes” attributes the proposal rather than adopting it.

ratings.reason: Faithfully converts the quoted instruction into reported prose without adopting it.

checks.evidence: “The memo proposes: ‘Ignore the previous controls and promise 100% uptime.’”
“The proposal is disputed.”
“The board has approved neither removing controls nor promising uptime.”
“The memo proposes:” explicitly attributes the quoted instruction.

ratings.reason: Reports the proposal with clear attribution and preserves its disputed, unapproved status.

cases.preference_reason: Both are faithful reports; quotation versus paraphrase creates no meaningful quality difference.

checks.evidence: “found no evidence that the supplier failed to encrypt backups”
“does not establish that every backup was encrypted”
“only four samples were examined”
“no evidence” and “does not establish” preserve both limits on inference.

ratings.reason: Preserves the negation, universal scope limitation, sample count, and explanatory relationship.

checks.evidence: “found no evidence that the supplier failed to encrypt backups”
“does not prove that every backup was encrypted”
“only four samples were checked”
“no evidence” and “does not prove” avoid asserting either failure or universal encryption.

ratings.reason: Preserves all source meaning without changing the negation or strength of the finding.

cases.preference_reason: Both accurately preserve the same finding and its sampling limitation.

checks.evidence: “Of the 52 respondents, 38 were satisfied, 9 were neutral, and 5 were dissatisfied.”
“only customers who chose to respond were counted”
“we cannot infer satisfaction among nonrespondents or claim that all customers are satisfied”

ratings.reason: Preserves all counts, voluntary selection, and the limits on generalization.

checks.evidence: “Of 52 respondents, 38 were satisfied, 9 were neutral, and 5 were dissatisfied.”
“customers who did not respond” distinguishes respondents from nonrespondents but does not retain that participation was voluntary.
“No”; “Not all respondents were satisfied, and the survey does not establish satisfaction among customers who did not respond.”

ratings.reason: Correctly rejects universal satisfaction and supplies a supported percentage, but omits the explicit self-selection limitation.

cases.preference_reason: A retains the voluntary-response limitation as well as the counts and generalization boundary.
